title: A cut matching the flow when no incrementing path exists
statement: Let $N$ be a network with a single source $x$ and a single sink $y$, and let $f$ be a flow in $N$. Suppose $N$ contains no $f$-incrementing path from $x$ to $y$ — that is, no path from the source to the sink each of whose arcs is either a forward arc that is not yet saturated ($f < c$) or a backward arc carrying positive flow ($f > 0$). Then there is a cut $(S,\bar S)$, a set of vertices with $x \in S$ and $y \notin S$, whose capacity equals the value of $f$: \[ \mathrm{val}(f) = \mathrm{cap}(S,\bar S). \]
hypotheses_covered: $N$ has no $f$-incrementing path reaching the sink $y$
caveat: The notion of an $f$-incrementing path is used in the statement but its formal definition is not included in the given snippet; it has been rendered in its standard (Ford–Fulkerson augmenting-path) sense.
replaced:
